🔥🇲🇽 <u>12 years after poisoning the Río Sonora, Larrea still won't pay</u>

Twelve years after Grupo México's mine dumped 40,000 m³ of acidified copper sulfate into the Río Sonora — the country's worst mining spill — Germán Larrea's conglomerate (co-owned with BlackRock) is still stalling on the final 500 million pesos it owes for cleanup, out of 1.5 billion agreed with the government. It has paid 1 billion. Sheinbaum's government set an Aug 21 deadline and threatened to reactivate criminal charges. The money funds water-treatment plants for the communities poisoned in 2014.
banner: RIO SONORA: MINE STILL OWES CLEANUP

🇲🇽🇨🇦 <u>Mexico and Canada want the USMCA renewed — now</u>

On an Aug 20 call, President Sheinbaum and Canadian PM Mark Carney agreed to push for renewing the T-MEC (USMCA) "lo antes posible" — as soon as possible — to give the region's businesses and workers certainty ahead of the 2026 review. Carney thanked Mexico for the 400+ firefighters it sent to battle Canada's summer wildfires. Two neighbors setting the terms together.

🇲🇽🩺 <u>Mexico makes free care for its #1 killer mandatory</u>

Mexico's Health Secretariat just made integrated care for "cardio-renal-metabolic syndrome" — diabetes, chronic kidney and heart disease — mandatory across IMSS, IMSS-Bienestar and ISSSTE. Together these cause 4 of every 10 deaths in the country, more than 300,000 a year. Free, public, and backed by the sugary-drink tax and the Healthy Schools program.
banner: MEXICO: FREE CARE VS ITS #1 KILLER

text: ‍REUTERS: Mexico Expects Trade Outcomes Similar to US-Canada Deal August 21, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Reuters ran Ebrard straight, no editorializing: Mexico expects terms "similar in many aspects" to the emerging US-Canada arrangement, pursuing "its own track with the United States." 🇲🇽 The context that survives the tariff-war headlines: Mexico is negotiating down a 25% auto tariff and a 50% steel tariff from leverage, not desperation — its economy still grew 2.7% year-on-year in July. • Ebrard: outcomes will be "similar in many aspects" to the US-Canada deal. • Mexico is pursuing "its own track with the United States."

‍LATIN TIMES: Sheinbaum Says "El Mayo" Case Remains Open After Witness Arrest August 21, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Mexico arrested Fausto Corrales, a key witness to how El Mayo Zambada was flown onto US soil in July 2024. The story US media files under cartel intrigue is, for Mexico, an unresolved abduction of a citizen across the border. 🇲🇽 Two years on, Sheinbaum keeps the file open — the question isn't the cartel, it's who put a man on a private plane to the United States. • "The investigations continue. This case has not been closed." — Sheinbaum • The arrest, called "relevant," aims to clarify what happened on July 25, 2024.
banner: El Mayo Case Still Open: Witness Held

text: ‍NYT/LA TIMES: Governor "Accused of Helping Cartel" Returns to Office August 21, 2026 | 🟡 📰 US outlets pegged Sinaloa Gov. Rocha Moya's return entirely to a Manhattan indictment — "wanted," "despite US charges." 🔍 The buried line: Mexico's own Attorney General found "not a shred of evidence" after 112 days of investigation. 🇲🇽 The unanswered ask: the DOJ has still not handed over the evidence behind its accusation. • "There is not a shred of evidence to support any claim of my involvement." — Rocha • "If they are accused, there must be evidence to support that accusation." — Sheinbaum • "The Foreign Ministry has repeatedly requested that the US provide the evidence." — Interior Secretariat

🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICO'S ECONOMY POSTS ITS BEST GROWTH IN OVER TWO YEARS</u>

Mexico's economy is on track for 2.7% annual growth in July — its strongest since March 2024 — driven by services up 2.8% (a 28-month high) and industry up 1.8%, according to INEGI's timely indicator (IOAE) reported by El Financiero. For January–July, activity is running at 1.5%, versus just 0.2% a year earlier. The collapse the business press keeps forecasting under the 4T still hasn't shown up.

🇲🇽🔭 <u>300 FREE TELESCOPES FOR THE RED MOON IN MEXICO CITY</u>

On August 27, all 300 of Mexico City's PILARES community centers will set up telescopes — free and open to everyone — to watch the partial lunar eclipse turn the moon red, with workshops on lunar phases and Mexico's own eclipse history. PILARES is the 4T's community-education network, built to put science in the neighborhoods that were always priced out of it.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MICHOACÁN: CJNG REGIONAL BOSS'S CELL DISMANTLED</u>

Federal forces captured nine members of a CJNG cell in Tanhuato and Ecuandureo, Michoacán — including regional leader Heraclio Guerrero, alias "Tío Lako," along with his daughter and his partner. The cell is blamed for attacks on the National Guard during the February 22 operation that killed CJNG chief "El Mencho." When gunmen blocked roads in retaliation, Plan Michoacán forces cleared them the same day and flew the nine to Mexico City for prosecution.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO CITY GOES AFTER THE PROPERTY-THEFT MAFIAS</u>

In just 12 days, Clara Brugada's Mexico City government detained 44 people for despojo — the violent seizure of people's homes — recovering some properties within two to three days. The strategy promises restitution within 15 days and a dedicated unit of 20 judges; on August 24 a Social Ombudsman office opens with 100 lawyers offering free legal defense. Chief Prosecutor Bertha Alcalde Luján says cases will be formalized within 30 days.
banner: CDMX: 44 HELD FOR HOME THEFT IN 12 DAYS
